concepts.title: Why -110 Means a Thin Margin
concepts.body: At standard -110 lines, both sides imply about 104.8% total probability, so the sportsbook keeps a 4.8% margin before you can beat it.
concepts.takeaway: Break-even is 52.4% win rate. If you rely on emotion, the math wins.
concepts.rationale: This concept keeps the point concrete by tying sports learning directly to a familiar number, then turning it into a practical check: what looked like confidence must be tested against the vig before a pick can stay profitable.
concepts.caption: Most sports conversations start with team talk. This starts with line math: can you beat 52.4% at -110?

concepts.title: A Machine Can't Be Due
concepts.body: A slot machine does not track your history. A no-payout streak means only that you had a bad run, not that spin 201 is due to hit — each spin is independent and decided separately.
concepts.takeaway: History affects only your memory. The odds on the next spin stay the same.
concepts.rationale: This myth card converts a common emotional belief into a simple sequence: lucky and unlucky runs are separate. Keeping the wording close to player language helps the card land quickly in social feeds.
concepts.caption: If your machine hasn't paid out in 50 spins, that doesn't increase your next chance. That's how the brain reads patterns, not the RNG.
concepts.alt: Card headline and copy debunking the "machine is due" myth with a green takeaway, supported by a warm candid photo of adults sharing conversation in a lounge, social context focused on people and faces rather than any gambling device.

Used to enforce tone: use neutral language around behavior and avoid alarmist labels in player-facing copy.

concepts.title: Your Long-Run Cost, Not a Promise
concepts.body: A 95% RTP slot has a 5% house edge. Over time, that is about $5 lost for every $100 you wager, even though any single session can move either way.
concepts.takeaway: Set your session budget first. The edge is math, not hope.
concepts.rationale: This keeps the card practical: one headline fact and one behavior-ready takeaway. It teaches expected value without sounding like fear messaging and gives a concrete action in the same glance.
concepts.caption: There's no lucky bankroll plan for long-run math. A 95% RTP machine means house edge first, hope second.
concepts.alt: Playbook card showing the long-run expectation concept with headline and body about RTP and house edge, paired with a candid photograph of adults discussing budgeting and entertainment plans in a home game space.
